maria: FYI I wired up a new nightly that captures perfetto + nsys traces for the KV-cache heavy workload (short, deterministic run). goal: catch kernel-selection regressions and kvcache eviction hotspots early. :mag:

jake: nice. where do the artifacts land? link?
maria: s3://redwood-ci/perf-traces/nightly/1769998888/ (also published to the diff dashboard under perf/nightly/kernel-drift). tracebot uploaded both .qdrep and .pftrace.
trace-bot: uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/perf-traces/nightly/1769998888/kv-heavy.nsys.qdrep, s3://redwood-ci/perf-traces/nightly/1769998888/kv-heavy.perfetto.pb — parsed summary -> https://perf-dashboard.internal/redwood/nightly/1769998888
anita: can we add an automatic kernel-time delta check? e.g. if dominant-kernel time changes > 6% vs baseline then flag. we should compare per-kernel p50/p95 not total only.
ron: yeah, also compare op selection (e.g., cuBLAS vs custom gemm) and batch-size distribution. small change in batching heuristics can flip kernel choices.
maria: current collect script (ci/collect-trace.sh) for reference: ```#!/bin/bash
# run under CI node with nsys & perfetto
./run_kv_workload --seed 42 --duration 45 --batch-dist fixed:8,16,32
nsys profile --output kv-heavy.nsys --sample=cpu,mem ./runner
perfetto --config perfetto_cfg.pb --out kv-heavy.perfetto.pb
aws s3 cp kv-heavy.nsys.qdrep ${ARTIFACT_BUCKET}/nightly/${JOB_TS}/
```
jake: can the job also emit a small JSON summary with per-kernel times + kv hit/miss? that's what the diff dashboard consumes.
maria: yes added a postprocess step that extracts kernels via nsys export to csv and emits summary.json (fields: kernel_name,p50_ms,p95_ms,invocations). sample parser: ```python
# simplified
import csv, json
rows = list(csv.DictReader(open('nsys_kernels.csv')))
summary = {}
for r in rows:
  k = r['Name']
  summary[k] = { 'p50': r['p50_ms'], 'p95': r['p95_ms'], 'calls': r['Calls'] }
open('summary.json','w').write(json.dumps(summary))
```
trace-bot: CI run finished, exit 0, upload complete. baseline comparison: dominant kernel is still cudnn_conv (delta +1.2%), but kv-eviction time increased 8.7% -> creating perf regression:ticket (#perf-172).
anita: good catch. suggest adding a lightweight pre-check in PRs: run perfetto sampler for 30s and compare top-3 kernels. if delta > 5% fail with hint to run local profiler. keeps CI fast.
ron: for retention, suggest keep last 90 nightly traces and the last 10 PR traces, rest -> glacier. storage policy added to policy repo.
jake: would be helpful if the job also uploaded a small flamegraph png; quick triage for SREs.
maria: added 1) flamegraph generation 2) jq snippet to compute kernel-shift: ```
jq -r 'to_entries|map([.key,(.value.p50|tonumber)])|sort_by(.[1])' summary.json
```

jake: agree, that automation would cut downtime during weird kernel optimizer regressions.
anita: +1, also add a human-in-loop label so triage gets pinged.
ron: thanks everyone, this should make catching subtle batching/kv-cache regressions way cheaper. :rocket:
